title: Star trails above the VLT
caption: Star trails above the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The four 8.2-metre Unit Telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope dominate this picture, while dotted star trails circle through the sky above them on Cerro Paranal.

The dotted trails record the apparent movement of the stars, but that movement is an illusion. It is Earth that turns as time passes, not the stars, and so the whole sky seems to rotate around the southern celestial pole. A sequence of photographs combined into one turns each star's slow drift into a line of dots.

This kind of picture is only possible with a very clear sky. The night above the 2600-metre-high summit in Chile's Atacama Desert is dark and clear enough that long sequences of photos can be taken without a single cloud passing in front of the stars. Clear skies like these also suit astronomers, whose observations of faint targets can last a long time.

understand.summary: This is a sequence of night-time photographs taken in visible light with a camera at Paranal and combined into one image. The exposure settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as fixed points. The dotted trails appear only because many separate exposures were combined.

explore: ESO describes the Very Large Telescope as an array, and all four of its large Unit Telescopes share this single mountaintop in the Atacama.
alt: Four large telescope enclosures beneath dotted star trails circling the sky.
